judgments.concern: The scenario names the pallet pose, the pallet width, height, and depth in metres, and which detected pallets are sent through stage 2 versus marked deferred. The handling process uses those while the scene can still change. face_attached_depth writes width and height as the factory face estimate_pose_chamfer_v3_2 already matches, params.pallet_width_m and params.pallet_height_m, and the search template stays that face. The scenario leaves that factory face as the pallet face. Writing those two sizes on the stage-2 outcome and on PalletPoseStamped after deferred_source_indices places that face on the pose result the handling process reads, beside the admitted source index and the deferred source indices published_admission_split already writes. The rich message already carries this pair's RGB and depth stamps, so the sizes belong to this capture. The face-centre position and yaw stay the pose, and pose.position.z stays the range of that centre. Depth is a length behind that face. Of the points sample_face_points already returned, project each with project_points_to_plane_2d, subtract best_pose.tx and best_pose.ty, and apply the inverse of the row map transform_points_2d uses, the same map at minus best_pose.theta_rad. Keep a point when those prototype coordinates lie inside the factory rectangle, absolute x at most half of pallet_width_m and absolute y at most half of pallet_height_m, closed on the boundary. The contribution is the negation of the signed point_to_plane_distance. orient_normal_toward_camera has already made the far side negative, so that negation is the length behind the face. Sort the kept contributions. Take the one closest to zero, the return nearest this face plane, and grow a window while each step to the next kept contribution is at most pallet_height_m. depth_m is the greatest contribution in that window. No second length is substituted, and no flag is written. sample_face_points keeps the depth returns inside the eroded detection bbox, so a point whose plane projection falls inside that factory rectangle can be the pallet body, a load, the floor, or another object. A later surface stays outside the window only when the step to it exceeds the face height. A load or another surface within one face height of the previous return is inside the window, and that farthest contribution is what the handling process would take as the pallet depth. A gap larger than the face height stops the window at the nearer cluster, so the published depth is that nearer length, including a window that never leaves the face plane. The factory face has width and height and no depth parameter. The scenario lists depth beside width and height, and lists the pose on its own. It states no rule that the far side of the mask returns inside that face, chained from the nearest return by steps of one face height, is the pallet depth. When no return falls inside the rectangle, the proposal names no depth and writes no flag, so a success can reach the handling process with the factory face and no body length. The rejected pocket_opening_depth took the median of far-side returns inside the two fork openings and set has_body_depth false when that set was empty. This proposal looks at the whole factory rectangle, takes the far side of the step-connected window, and writes no flag. The rejected inlier_face_extents took depth as the mean z of the plane inliers, which is the pose range. This depth is a length behind the face. The user named the three sizes. The part they did not name is that width and height are the factory face this match already used, and that depth is the far side of the returns inside that face which stay within one face-height step of the face plane. Stage 2 still runs once, on the one candidate the admission split already admits. A failed estimate publishes no PalletPoseStamped, and the failure diagnostic stays the admission lists it already carries. The two early returns in on_pair stay silent.

The scenario names the pallet width, height, and depth in metres separately from the pallet pose, for the pallet the vehicle handles while the scene can still change. fork_opening_depth writes width as params.pallet_width_m and height as params.pallet_height_m, the factory face cached_prototype already passes to build_default_pallet_prototype, and the search template stays that face. The scenario leaves that factory face as the pallet face. Those two sizes are written on the stage-2 outcome and on PalletPoseStamped after deferred_source_indices, so they sit on the pose result with the admission split this capture already publishes. The face-centre position and yaw stay the pose, and pose.position.z stays centre_r.z(), the range lift_point_from_plane_2d and apply_se3 already store for the face centre. The two fork openings are the pocket centres build_default_pallet_prototype already cuts, at minus and plus pocket_centre_offset_m along the prototype width axis. Those centres are placed with transform_points_2d at best_pose, lifted with lift_point_from_plane_2d on the same plane basis as the face centre, and mapped into the camera RGB optical frame with apply_se3. They lie on the face plane. Depth is the mean of those two centres' z in that RGB frame. On a frontal face the two centres share the face centre's optical depth, so depth_m is the range already stored as pose.position.z. On a tilted face the two optical depths differ, and their mean is still the range of two points on the face, while pose.position.z remains the face centre. The scenario lists depth with width and height, and lists the pose on its own, so the optical range of the face is the pose's range. The factory face has width and height and no depth parameter. The handling process would size the approach from a camera range of the openings this match placed, including a capture whose depth returns never measured a body behind the face. The two centres are also written on the outcome and, after depth_m, on PalletPoseStamped, the negative-offset centre first. The scenario names the pose, the three sizes, and which detections are sent through stage 2 versus marked deferred. It states no rule that the optical depth of the two fork-opening centres is the pallet depth, and no rule that those two centres are a result the handling process reads. The rejected pocket_opening_depth measured a median far-side length through the openings from sample_face_points and could withhold that length when the openings showed no body. This proposal does not read those returns. It lifts the prototype hole centres onto the plane and publishes their optical depth on every success. The rejected inlier_face_extents took depth as the mean z of the plane inliers, the pose range. This proposal takes the mean optical z of two points on that same face. The user named the three sizes. The part they did not name is that depth is the optical depth of the two fork openings this match already cuts, and that those two centres are on the pose result. The rich message already carries this pair's RGB and depth stamps, so the message is this capture, while the depth value is the range of the prototype openings on this face. Stage 2 still runs once, on the one candidate the admission split already admits. A failed estimate publishes no PalletPoseStamped, and the failure diagnostic stays the admission lists it already carries. The two early returns in on_pair stay silent.

The scenario names the pallet width, height, and depth in metres separately from the pallet pose, for the pallet the vehicle handles while the scene can still change, and it names which detected pallets are sent through stage 2 versus marked deferred. published_face_sizes writes width and height as the prototype face, params.pallet_width_m and params.pallet_height_m, the sizes cached_prototype already passes to build_default_pallet_prototype. The search template stays that face. The scenario leaves that factory face as the pallet face. Writing width_m and height_m on the stage-2 outcome and on PalletPoseStamped after deferred_source_indices places that face on the pose result the handling process reads, beside the admitted source index and the deferred source indices published_admission_split already writes. The face-centre position and yaw stay the pose. Depth is the face-centre range this call already stores as pose.tz. lift_point_from_plane_2d and apply_se3 produce centre_r, and centre_r.z() is the z of that centre in the camera RGB optical frame. publish_pose already copies that scalar into pose.position.z. The same scalar is depth_m. has_dimensions is set true on that success, and publish_pose copies the flag with the three scalars onto the rich message. The scenario lists depth with width and height, and lists the pose on its own. Face-centre range is the pose's range. Copying it into depth_m gives the handling process that range a second time under the size the scenario lists beside width and height. The factory face has width and height and no depth parameter. has_dimensions is true on every success that publishes PalletPoseStamped. A failed estimate leaves the flag false and publishes no PalletPoseStamped, so the handling process never reads the flag as a missing body. The scenario states no rule that the optical-frame z of the face centre is the pallet depth, and no rule that a flag true on every published pose marks the three sizes. The rejected inlier_face_extents took depth as the mean z of the plane inliers after the same depth-to-RGB transform, which is that face range. This proposal publishes the single face-centre z. The user named the three sizes. The part they did not name is that width and height are the prototype face this match already uses, and that depth is that estimated optical-frame z, written with those sizes on the pose result. The rich message already carries this pair's RGB and depth stamps, so the message is this capture, while the depth value is the pose range this capture already carries. Stage 2 still runs once, on the one candidate the pose node admits. A failed estimate publishes no PalletPoseStamped, and the failure diagnostic stays the admission lists it already carries. The two early returns in on_pair stay silent.
